item.text: {"analysis":"The experiment succeeded on host validation: macro HR@10 reached 0.535, improving by 0.0225 over the previous 0.5125 and by 0.0300 over baseline 0.505. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.550, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.575, Electronics 0.450, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.565. Movies_and_TV recovered from the reported previous 0.515, but remained below its earlier 0.580. The isolated change supports ten-transition recency weighting with per-prefix normalization for this configuration: recent transitions receive more supervision while each sampled prefix retains total weight 1/batch_size. One validation run does not establish generalization or identify which categories caused the aggregate improvement beyond the supplied comparisons. No test results were available.","code_summary":"Trains one independent bias-enabled SASRec per category, selecting and loading exactly one checkpoint for each route. Each network uses tied 64-dimensional item embeddings, learned positions, two causal attention blocks with one head, residual feed-forward layers, dropout 0.5, and jointly trained item biases. Dense unsmoothed sampled cross-entropy uses 32 uniform negatives excluding training-history items, float32 scoring, and checkpointed chunks of 512 positions. The sole experimental change weights valid transitions by 2^(-d/10), where d counts valid transitions after the position, then normalizes within each prefix and divides by batch size. Sampling, optimizer, seeds, epoch limit, validation, early stopping, predictor writer, and inference scoring remain unchanged. No ensembles, checkpoint averaging, or separately fitted scorers are used."}
